title: ISACA CDPSE
summary: The Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer (CDPSE) is an ISACA certification for experienced privacy and technology professionals who build privacy into systems rather than only writing policy. It sits at a mid to senior level, aimed at engineers, architects, auditors, and privacy programme staff with several years of relevant work. It proves to an employer that you can design privacy controls, assess data handling risk, and manage retention across the full data lifecycle in line with laws such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). The exam uses multiple choice questions covering three domains, and ISACA also requires qualifying work experience. ISACA has announced a revision of this exam, so the domain structure below follows the long established published objectives and omits weightings that cannot be confirmed; check the vendor's current exam content outline before booking. It leads to roles such as privacy engineer, data protection officer support, security architect, and privacy programme manager. This is an independent study guide, not official ISACA material.

beginner.definition: The Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer (CDPSE) is a certification from ISACA. It is for people who build and check the systems that keep personal data safe. It is not only about writing privacy rules. It is about making privacy work inside real technology.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many laws now say that companies must protect personal data. Companies need people who can turn those laws into working controls. This certificate shows an employer that you can do that. It helps you move from a general security role into privacy work. It also proves that you understand both the legal side and the technical side.
howItWorks: Read the official ISACA exam outline first, so you know the three domains and what each one asks of you.
Study privacy law basics, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which is the data law of the European Union.
Learn how privacy controls are built into systems, including data mapping and consent records.
Practise with a question bank that explains answers, so you learn the reasoning and not just the fact.
Book the exam when your practice scores are steady, then review weak domains in the last week.
The exam itself is multiple choice, taken at a test centre or online, and it tests judgement more than memory.
beginner.example: Think of a hospital that stores patient records. A doctor needs the full history to treat a patient. A billing clerk needs only the name and the payment details. A privacy engineer looks at that system and asks who can see what, how long each record is kept, and what happens when it is deleted. The engineer then sets rules in the software so the billing clerk simply cannot open the full history. That is the kind of work this certification is about.
takeaways: CDPSE is aimed at experienced people, so check the work experience requirement before you pay for the exam.
You need both legal knowledge and technical skill, so do not skip either side.
Learn to read the exam outline closely, because it tells you exactly which domains are tested.

objectives: Describe how privacy governance fits with an organisation's overall risk and compliance work
Explain the main duties that data protection law places on a company that handles personal data
Identify where personal data is collected, moved, stored and shared across a business
Judge the privacy risk of a new system or a change to an existing one
Select technical controls such as encryption, masking and access limits for personal data
Plan retention and deletion rules that match legal duties and business needs

chapters.title: Privacy governance
objectives: Build a privacy programme that matches the size and risk of the organisation
Write and maintain a record of processing activities that stays accurate over time
Assign privacy duties to named owners and prove that they are carried out
Run privacy training and awareness that changes real behaviour
Monitor privacy controls and report the results to senior management

chapters.title: Privacy architecture
objectives: Map the flow of personal data through applications, storage and third parties
Apply privacy by design and by default when a system is first built
Choose technical controls such as encryption, tokenisation and access limits
Review the privacy risk of cloud services and external suppliers
Assess how new technology such as analytics or machine learning affects personal data

chapters.title: Data lifecycle
objectives: Set rules for collecting only the personal data that is truly needed
Define retention periods and explain the legal reason for each one
Carry out secure deletion and prove that the data is really gone
Handle requests from people who ask to see, correct or erase their data
Manage personal data in backups, archives and test environments
